phases.title: Motor de deploy — runtime
phases.goal: Through the API a person creates project → environment → service (Git, Dockerfile or image, public or private) on a connected server and deploys it in the worker with live build logs, real container state, cancellation that kills the remote process, cleanup on every exit and honest reconciliation; 20 deploys and 20 create/delete cycles leave nothing orphaned.

tasks.title: Domain: project, environment and service inputs

acceptance.text: Project name and slug derivation (unique-safe, lowercase, collision suffix is the caller's job) and optional description validated into branded types
Environment name validator accepts any valid name; production/staging/development exported as suggestions only, kind stays free text (D23)

Service create/edit input validators for git (url, branch, context, Dockerfile, optional target), image (tag or digest, never implicit :latest), internal port and optional published port; no build-arg or env fields exist (D13)
classifyServiceEdit() pure: says whether an edit changes the source (requires redeploy) or only metadata
>=95% statement and branch coverage on the new validators; domain purity test still green

Git URL validator accepts only https:// and ssh (scp-style or ssh://) after parsing; rejects file:, ext::, git://, http://, javascript:/data:, embedded userinfo credentials, and values starting with '-' or containing whitespace/control chars

Branch, context path and Dockerfile path validators reject '..' segments, absolute paths, leading '-', NUL/newline and over-long values; image ref validator rejects whitespace, leading '-' and malformed digests

Slug derivation handles empty result (all non-ASCII/symbols), Unicode normalization, max length and reserved words with a deterministic fallback; ports validated as integers in 1-65535 and published port not equal to internal-only reserved ports

tasks.title: Domain: runtime policies (resource ledger, port preflight, reconcile diff, post-start polls)

acceptance.text: Resource ledger records workspace, per-attempt image, network, container and secrets file, and returns the cleanup set for each exit (SUCCESS, FAILED, CANCELLED, timeout, WORKER_CRASHED); the per-service running container is never in a failed attempt's cleanup set
Port preflight rejects collisions with other services on the server, the panel ports and ports in the parsed docker ps snapshot, returning PORT_IN_USE with the conflicting owner
Reconcile diff maps one docker ps snapshot to per-service container states, reports only changed services, and flags containers stopped or removed outside Noodara as discrepancies
Post-start poll schedule is 5 polls with 1 s to 8 s backoff, parameterised, and decides SUCCESS / START_FAILED / keep polling from inspect results
>=95% statement and branch coverage on the four modules
Resource ledger cleanup set is idempotent: computing and executing it twice yields the same set and a second run on already-removed resources is not an error

tasks.title: Domain: build-log chunker and runtime-log sanitizer

acceptance.text: Chunker flushes on time or size (defaults 250 ms / 16 KB, injected clock), assigns a monotonic seq per deployment and phase
Per-line cap (16 KB) truncates UTF-8-safely with a visible marker; per-phase cap (10 MiB) stops accepting and emits one truncation notice
Sanitizer strips ANSI escapes and replaces binary / invalid UTF-8 with a placeholder; never throws on arbitrary bytes (property test)
No I/O, no timers owned by the module; >=95% coverage

tasks.title: Deploy env knobs and deploy job budget

acceptance.text: Knobs NOODARA_DEPLOY_MAX_MS, NOODARA_DEPLOY_IDLE_MS, NOODARA_DEPLOY_CONCURRENCY, NOODARA_DEPLOY_LOG_MAX_BYTES, NOODARA_DEPLOY_LOG_FLUSH_MS/BYTES, NOODARA_DEPLOY_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS, NOODARA_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS, NOODARA_RUNTIME_LOG_TAIL, NOODARA_RUNTIME_LOG_FOLLOW_MAX_MS with research defaults and range validation
Every knob listed in turbo.json passThroughEnv and documented in .env.example (ADR 0003)
Deploy lock duration and Redis cancel-key TTL derived from NOODARA_DEPLOY_MAX_MS so BullMQ never reaps a live build (unit-tested at min and max)
Cross-knob validation: IDLE_MS <= MAX_MS, FLUSH_BYTES <= per-line cap, LOG_MAX_BYTES >= phase cap; invalid combinations fail boot with a named error without echoing unrelated env values

tasks.title: Activity actions and SSE event surface for projects, services and deployments

acceptance.text: Activity actions for project, environment, service and deployment lifecycle (incl. out-of-band container change) with metadata allowlists that cannot carry secrets
SSE surface is exactly service.updated, service.deleted, deployment.updated, deployment.log_chunk added to the server events (D22); no project.* or environment.* events
deployment.log_chunk payload is bounded and carries deploymentId, phase, seq; backpressure eviction behaviour of sse-broadcaster unchanged (existing tests green)

tasks.title: HTTPS-token clone contract test and askpass secret slot

acceptance.text: Askpass helper gets its own secret file name under <ws>/secrets (no longer the known_hosts slot), mode 600, removed with the workspace
Fixture serves an HTTPS (or HTTP basic-auth) git remote; clone with a token via askpass succeeds on 22.04 and 24.04, wrong token gives REPOSITORY_AUTH_FAILED
Token absent from ps, .git/config, remote URL and every captured stream
ADR 0008 open item 4 updated with the measured result

Deploy keys, HTTPS tokens and registry passwords never reach argv, URLs, env-over-SSH, logs, API responses, activity metadata or error messages; every streamed chunk goes through the Redactor; a per-run canary asserts it

tasks.title: Projects and environments API

acceptance.text: Create, edit, list and read projects (unique name case-insensitive, slug derived) and environments (unique per project); duplicates give a named 409

Archive and unarchive; delete only an archived project by typing its exact name (422 otherwise); the DB cascade covers environments, services, deployments, log chunks and service credentials (remote cleanup arrives in 12-14)
Environment routes reject an environment id from another project (404, no existence leak)
Every mutation writes an activity event; routes behind requireSession and origin guard like servers.ts

Malformed JSON, wrong content-type, unknown fields and oversized bodies on project/environment routes return 400/413/422 and the API keeps serving; name uniqueness race (two parallel creates differing only in case) yields one 201 and one named 409, never a 500
Project and environment endpoints return 401 without session and 403 on cross-origin mutation; unauthenticated requests never reveal whether an id exists

tasks.title: Services API: create, edit, read with derived status and guards

acceptance.text: Create git and image services only on a CONNECTED server with Docker; Dockerfile (git) services rejected when docker_buildkit_available is false (ADR 0008 G3)
Published port optional and off by default; collisions with other services on the server and the panel ports give PORT_IN_USE at create/edit time
Read returns every SVC-05 field with status from deriveServiceStatus (never a hand-written value); edit flags requiresRedeploy when the source changes
No route accepts a service, environment or server id outside the path's project; covered by a cross-project ownership test
Create and edit write activity events and publish service.updated

Service create/edit routes enforce body cap and reject malformed JSON with explicit 4xx; git URL scheme allowlist and path validators from 12-01 are applied server-side (not only in UI) and violations return a named 422

Port collision check at create/edit is race-safe: two concurrent creates claiming the same published port on one server result in exactly one success (DB-level constraint or lock), the other PORT_IN_USE

tasks.title: Private source credentials and delete-server guard

acceptance.text: Noodara generates an ed25519 deploy key per service, stores the private half encrypted at rest, returns only the public key
HTTPS token and registry password accepted write-only, encrypted at rest, never returned (responses expose only presence and type)
Credentials are rotated or removed when the source changes and deleted with the service (no orphan credentials rows)
Deleting a server with services returns 409 naming the blocking services (PROJ-05)

Deploy keys, HTTPS tokens and registry passwords never reach argv, URLs, env-over-SSH, logs, API responses, activity metadata or error messages; every streamed chunk goes through the Redactor; a per-run canary asserts it

Credential encryption uses authenticated encryption with a fresh random nonce per write; ciphertext tamper is detected on decrypt; deploy keys are generated with node:crypto (no Math.random) and each service gets a distinct key
Credential store never exposes plaintext through toJSON/inspect/error serialization; decrypt failures surface a closed-vocabulary code without ciphertext or key material

Credential inputs are validated server-side: token and registry password length capped, registry host and username validated, request body capped (413) and malformed JSON rejected (400) without echoing the submitted secret

tasks.title: Deploy queue and enqueue / read API

acceptance.text: POST /api/services/:id/deploy inserts a QUEUED deployment (source snapshot) and enqueues jobId deploy-<deploymentId>, answering immediately
A second deploy while one is active returns 409 DEPLOYMENT_IN_PROGRESS via the partial unique index, also under a concurrent race (two parallel POSTs, exactly one 201)
Archived project blocks deploys with a named error
GET deployment list per service (paginated, newest first) and detail; payload contains ids only, never secrets

If enqueue fails after the QUEUED insert (Redis down), the deployment is moved to FAILED with a named code or the insert is rolled back; no deployment stays QUEUED without a job; API answers a named 503, not a crash
Deployment list pagination caps page size (upper bound validated) and rejects malformed cursors/limits with 4xx; reading a deployment of another service/project returns 404
Deploy, cancel and other POST routes enforce the Fastify body cap (413) and reject unknown fields (422)

tasks.title: Deploy job pipeline: clone, build or pull, preflight, start, verify, cleanup

acceptance.text: Worker clones --depth 1 into /opt/noodara-deploy/<deploymentId> (SHA captured), builds noodara/<serviceId>:<deploymentId> with optional target, or pulls the image (registry login via --password-stdin into the per-deployment --config)
Port preflight against real docker ps; then old container replaced by noodara-<serviceId> on noodara-net-<serviceId> with --log-opt max-size/max-file; post-start polls decide SUCCESS or START_FAILED
Statuses move only through the domain state machine (QUEUED→PREPARING→BUILDING→DEPLOYING→SUCCESS/FAILED); service status cache recomputed and service.updated / deployment.updated published
failing-build ends FAILED/BUILD_FAILED with the previous container still running; max vs idle timeout give BUILD_TIMEOUT vs BUILD_STALLED

Ledger cleanup on every exit removes workspace, secrets, partial image and half-created container/network; superseded image removed after the new container runs; images compared by digest or RootFS.Layers, never .Id (ADR 0008)
Log output goes through an injected sink interface (real sink in 12-12)
SSH, Docker or Git failures surface as a closed-vocabulary code with an actionable message; raw remote stderr never reaches an API response and no remote failure crashes the API or the worker

Deploy keys, HTTPS tokens and registry passwords never reach argv, URLs, env-over-SSH, logs, API responses, activity metadata or error messages; every streamed chunk goes through the Redactor; a per-run canary asserts it
Worker job is idempotent against BullMQ stall/retry: a re-delivered job for a deployment already past QUEUED does not re-run remote commands (attempts 1 or state guard), proven by a stalled-job test

Per-deployment workspace path, image tag and container/network names are built only from validated ids; repo-controlled values (branch, Dockerfile path, git output) are never interpolated into shell strings, proven with hostile names ($(), backticks, ';', leading '-') in a fixture repo

tasks.title: Build log pipeline: redact, persist, publish, resync, retention

acceptance.text: Every chunk passes the Redactor before persistence, Redis or SSE; a secret split across chunks never leaks
Chunks persisted append-only in deployment_log_chunks with seq, flushed on the 12-03 cadence, capped per line and per phase
deployment.log_chunk reaches an SSE client live during a node-api build; GET /api/deployments/:id/logs?since=<seq> returns only later chunks (no replay)
Retention job deletes chunks older than NOODARA_DEPLOY_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS without touching the deployment rows
A fixture that logs continuously for minutes keeps API RSS and SSE buffers bounded (no eviction of a healthy client); numbers recorded

Deploy keys, HTTPS tokens and registry passwords never reach argv, URLs, env-over-SSH, logs, API responses, activity metadata or error messages; every streamed chunk goes through the Redactor; a per-run canary asserts it

Log persistence failure (DB error) or Redis publish failure is logged without chunk content and does not fail or stall the deployment; seq has a unique constraint per deployment and phase and duplicate inserts are rejected
GET /api/deployments/:id/logs validates since as a non-negative integer, caps page size, requires session and returns 404 for deployments outside the caller's scope

tasks.title: Cancellation and worker-crash sweep

acceptance.text: Cancelling a QUEUED deployment removes the job and ends CANCELLED; it never executes any remote command

Cancelling a running build: Redis flag (TTL from 12-04) → killSupervisedOperation (kill -s TERM -- "-$pgid" under setsid -w, ADR 0008) → confirmed absence in ps → channel destroyed → cleanup → CANCELLED; only the worker transitions
After cancel no container, partial image, network, workspace or secrets file remains and docker system df is unchanged
Worker killed mid-build: startup sweep marks FAILED/WORKER_CRASHED, cleans per-deployment resources, never the per-service container
SSH, Docker or Git failures surface as a closed-vocabulary code with an actionable message; raw remote stderr never reaches an API response and no remote failure crashes the API or the worker

Cancel is idempotent and race-safe: cancelling a terminal deployment returns a named 409, a second cancel during CANCELLING is a no-op, and cancel racing with SUCCESS leaves exactly one terminal state

If killSupervisedOperation cannot confirm absence, deployment still ends FAILED/CANCEL_UNCONFIRMED-style named code with cleanup attempted and a warning activity event; the worker does not hang past a bounded timeout

tasks.title: Service operations and deletion with remote cleanup

acceptance.text: Redeploy, stop, restart and remove are timed jobs that write activity events and publish service.updated
Deleting a service (exact name) stops and removes its container, network, own images and workspace, then its credentials and rows; service.deleted published
Deleting an archived project runs the same remote cleanup for every service before the DB cascade; an unreachable server leaves a named error, not orphaned rows pointing nowhere
Operations on a service with an active deployment return 409 DEPLOYMENT_IN_PROGRESS
SSH, Docker or Git failures surface as a closed-vocabulary code with an actionable message; raw remote stderr never reaches an API response and no remote failure crashes the API or the worker

Service delete is resumable and idempotent: a failure midway (SSH drop) leaves the service row with a named error and re-running the delete completes cleanup without errors on already-removed resources
Delete confirmation compares the exact name server-side; wrong/missing confirmation returns 422 and performs no remote command
Service operation and delete routes enforce the body cap (413), validate the confirmation field length and reject unknown fields (422)

tasks.title: Reconciliation tick

acceptance.text: Repeatable job every NOODARA_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS runs one docker ps --size=false per CONNECTED server, never per service, with commandMs timeout
Changed container state updates the cached service status and emits service.updated; unchanged state emits nothing
A container stopped or removed outside Noodara shows in the next tick and writes one activity event (no repeat on later ticks)
An unreachable server marks its services UNKNOWN, never STOPPED, and does not crash the tick for other servers
Reconcile ticks never overlap (a slow tick delays the next rather than running concurrently) and skip services with an active deployment so they cannot overwrite in-flight status

tasks.title: Runtime logs on demand

acceptance.text: GET tail returns the last N lines (default NOODARA_RUNTIME_LOG_TAIL, upper bound validated) with timestamps
Follow is a dedicated bounded stream (not a new global SSE type) that ends at NOODARA_RUNTIME_LOG_FOLLOW_MAX_MS and when the client disconnects, killing the remote docker logs
Output is redacted and sanitized (ANSI, binary) and never persisted
SSH, Docker or Git failures surface as a closed-vocabulary code with an actionable message; raw remote stderr never reaches an API response and no remote failure crashes the API or the worker
Concurrent follow streams are capped per server and per user with a named 429/409; tail validates N as a positive integer within the upper bound and rejects other values with 4xx

tasks.title: Leak canaries for the deploy engine

acceptance.text: Canaries for git-URL token, deploy key, registry password and a fixture build that prints a canary
Absence asserted in build logs, deployment_log_chunks, SSE stream, activity_events.metadata, every API response, docker inspect, docker history and the remote .git/config
pnpm security:scan-leaks includes the new file

Deploy keys, HTTPS tokens and registry passwords never reach argv, URLs, env-over-SSH, logs, API responses, activity metadata or error messages; every streamed chunk goes through the Redactor; a per-run canary asserts it

tasks.title: QA-08 soak: 20 deploys and 20 create/delete cycles

acceptance.text: 20 consecutive node-api deployments complete SUCCESS
20 service create/delete cycles leave no container, network, image or workspace; docker system df equal before and after, twice in a row without manual prune
Nightly runs the soak on 22.04 and 24.04 (NOODARA_SOAK=1) and fails on any surviving noodara.test=true resource
Soak records per-iteration duration and docker system df before/after to an artifact so leak regressions are visible, and fails when any iteration exceeds the deploy max timeout

docs/deploy-engine.md describes the API surface, statuses, error codes and knobs in under two pages
